newsitem.title: UK: UK will not join EMU if criteria fudged - Major.
newsitem.headline: UK will not join EMU if criteria fudged - Major.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Sunday they the UK would not join European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) if other nations fudge the convergence criteria.
"If they are fudging the criteria there would be no question of the UK joining," he told BBC Television.
However, he said Britain intends to stay in the EMU discussions and not abandon the wait-and-see policy.
Major said if other countries were fudging the single currency convergence criteria "then I need to be at the table to argue against that".

Major has been forced to forge a compromise between Eurosceptics on the right of the Conservative Party who want him to rule out membership of EMU, and his pro-European finance minister Kenneth Clarke who is insisting that Britain's options remain open.
The government denied press reports last week that Major was planning to effectively rule out EMU membership in the life of the next Parliament.
Major also refused to comment on whether Britain would be among the first wave of countries to form EMU in 1999.
When asked if Britain would join the first wave of EMU he said, "I am not going to get drawn into (answering that question)".

He said Britain would remain part of the EU but would not be pulled along with it if he thought it were moving in the wrong direction. Major said reports that he would abandon the government's wait-and-see policy were "just not true".
